IMPLEMENTATION VALIDATED (structural half). Standard/mid tier (sonnet) implementer; the live half cannot run on this arm64 host by design and comes from CI after landing.
FILES: tests/external/live_jira_dc/{Dockerfile,docker-compose.yml,conftest.py,README.md} + my test_harness_smoke.py; tests/unit/rebar_reconciler/test_jira_dc_harness_shape.py; a new 'jira-dc-harness' job in external-integration.yml (line 263) modelled on langfuse-trace; the --ignore=tests/external/live_jira_dc flag on the pre-existing external job (line 151); Makefile jira-dc-up/down + .PHONY.
VERIFIED: docker build SUCCEEDS. 'pytest --collect-only -m "not integration and not external" tests/external/live_jira_dc/' collects ZERO (4 deselected). Harness suite skips cleanly with no opt-in; with REBAR_RUN_EXTERNAL=1 and no instance it skips AND the canary correctly prints 'collected=4 executed=0 ... validated nothing' — so the _live_jira_ready sentinel wiring and the all-skip guard both work end-to-end. make typecheck GREEN (389 files). make lint GREEN after I fixed one E501 in MY OWN smoke test.

MY HELD-OUT ORACLE CAUGHT NOTHING IN THE IMPLEMENTATION — but MUTATION CAUGHT TWO HOLES IN MY ORACLE, which is the more useful result:
 1. FALSE POSITIVE: my loopback assertion FAILED against CORRECT config. The compose file is right ('127.0.0.1:2990:2990'); my regex matched '2990:2990' from inside the COMMENT that warns against that very anti-pattern. Well-commented config quotes the thing it forbids, so raw-text scanning of a structured file is wrong by construction. Rewrote to parse the YAML and assert on services.<name>.ports / platform / tty / stdin_open as PARSED values.
 2. HOLLOW ASSERTION: deleting '-Dproduct.start.timeout=2700000' from the ENTRYPOINT still PASSED, because my check was 'flag in text' and the flag name appears in the Dockerfile comments — comments I had myself required in a sibling AC. My two requirements defeated each other: requiring documentation made the presence check unfalsifiable. Rewrote to assert against the ENTRYPOINT/CMD INSTRUCTION with comment lines stripped.
 Both fixes then mutation-verified: bare 2990:2990 => RED; tty removed => RED; digest unpinned => RED; timeout flag removed from entrypoint => RED; skipAllPrompts removed => RED. Restored => 13/13 green.
CONSOLIDATION: the implementer independently wrote its own structural test (10 tests). Rather than pick one, I merged — kept mine (YAML parsing + instruction-level precision, both mutation-proven) and PORTED FOUR assertions it had that mine lacked: the two dud flags must NOT appear on the entrypoint; the unpublished pycontribs image must not be a source; compose must 'build:' locally; compose must mount a persistent /root/.m2. Its file deleted, coverage strictly increased, 13 tests total. The m2-mount addition was itself teeth-checked (removing the mount => RED).
NOTE: 'my oracle found no implementation defect' is a real result here, not a null one — the brief carried every hard-won fact (both mandatory flags, the two dud names, the digest, loopback, TTY, 8.x-only) because I had already paid for them in three failed runs. The oracle's value this time was catching MY errors.
